READ THE DATA RESPONSIBLY

Context matters.

PISA tests how 15-year-old students apply knowledge. Scores are scale points, not percentages. Comparing scores between different subjects does not measure which subject students are “better at”.

National means conceal differences within countries. These data cannot establish what caused a change or assess any individual school. Questionnaire associations, including AI use, do not establish causation.

Coverage & comparability

This snapshot uses the OECD results released on 8 September 2026. It is manually curated and is not a live OECD feed. Some countries and subjects are missing. A missing entry is not a statement about participation or performance.

Vietnam switched to computer-based assessment in 2025. The OECD excludes it from performance-trend analysis because comparability with earlier cycles is uncertain.

Map colours use fixed descriptive bands chosen for this site. They are not OECD proficiency levels. Point gaps are calculated from rounded mean scores.
